idea: Routines & independence #2 – getting dressed for the cold (HOUSE OUTSIDE, on the porch by the round red front door): the very first snowflakes of the season fall and a big sparkly snowflake lands right on Baby Ava's nose ('Oh! A snowflake! Brrr! So cold!'); chorus 'Jacket, hat and mittens! Warm, warm, warm!'; she dresses herself step by step – 'My jacket on! Zip, zip, zip!', 'My hat on my head! Pull it down!', 'Mittens on my hands! Clap, clap, clap!'; 'I did it myself!'; she asks the viewer 'What goes on my head? Hmm?' (pause) – 'My hat! Yay! Warm and cozy!'; lesson 'Dress up warm when it is cold!'. Loop: the hook framing again, the snowflake on her nose, now fully dressed and giggling, bye-bye wave with her pink mitten.
lesson: Getting dressed by yourself for cold weather: jacket, hat, mittens – dress up warm when it is cold.
place: HOUSE OUTSIDE (reference image house.jpg) – the small porch in front of the round red front door with the star-shaped window
calendar: Thursday slot 2 – Routines & independence (#1 tidy up on 5 Nov; today: getting dressed for the cold, seasonal: first snowflakes in November).

variety.outfit: HOME (shot 1) -> WINTER, put on piece by piece

characters: BABY AVA: a cute chubby 1-year-old baby girl with short fluffy curly brown hair, one small curly ponytail on top with a sparkly pink star hair clip, big brown eyes, rosy cheeks. wearing a soft yellow dress with ruffle sleeves and a small pink flower, and pink baby shoes with bows.
(from shot 2 on, put on step by step) wearing a puffy pink jacket, a yellow knitted hat with a pompom and pink mittens.
setting: HOUSE OUTSIDE: a cozy two-story pastel yellow house with a blue roof, white windows with flower boxes, a round red front door with a star-shaped window, a small porch with two lanterns, a stone path across green grass, a white picket fence and flower beds. (+ the very first tiny snowflakes drifting, grass still green)

learning.goal: Name three warm clothes and put them on in order by yourself when it is cold: jacket, hat, mittens.
learning.shown_how: Shot 2 Ava zips up her puffy pink jacket; shot 3 she pulls the yellow pompom hat down onto her head; shot 4 she claps in pink mittens. Each item appears only in its own shot, in the same order as the song.
learning.interactive_moment: 0:18-0:21 'What goes on my head? Hmm?' + 0:21-0:23 humming pause (question boing) -> 0:23 'My hat! Yay!' + cheer + confetti
learning.copy_me: 0:06 zip up your jacket 'Zip, zip, zip!' · 0:09 pull your hat down · 0:12 clap your hands 'Clap, clap, clap!'
learning.fact_check: Jacket on the body, hat on the head, mittens on the hands – correct. Snowflake drawn as a six-pointed snow crystal. No text, letters or numbers in any frame.
learning.modeling: Ava feels cold in her dress and fixes it herself by dressing warm before playing outside; independence line 'I did it myself!'. Correct behaviour throughout.
learning.toddler_fit: Simple words, bright soft daylight, gentle snowflakes, nothing scary, one baby, big face.

fun_mechanics: surprise hook: a snowflake lands on her nose
say-it-with-me chorus: Jacket, hat and mittens!
copy-me: zip, pull the hat down, clap
interactive pause: What goes on my head?

title: Brrr! It's Snowing! ❄️ Jacket, Hat & Mittens with Baby Ava | Get Dressed for Winter | Crayon Babies
description:
Oh! A snowflake lands on Baby Ava's nose! ❄️ Brrr, it's cold! Sing along with Baby Ava as she gets dressed all by herself to stay warm: jacket, hat and mittens.

🎬 What happens in this video:
😮 "Oh! A snowflake! Brrr! So cold!"
🧥 My jacket on! Zip, zip, zip!
🧶 My hat on my head! Pull it down!
🧤 Mittens on my hands! Clap, clap, clap!
🤔 "What goes on my head?" – can you answer?
👋 Dress up warm when it is cold! Bye bye, friends!

📚 Kids learn: getting dressed by yourself • jacket • hat • mittens • warm and cold • winter clothes

🎶 Voices only: children singing, humming and clapping with a soft hand drum – no other musical instruments.

A cozy sing-along getting-dressed song for toddlers and preschoolers, with Baby Ava on the porch of the Crayon House when the first snowflakes fall – she zips up her jacket, pulls on her hat and claps in her mittens, all by herself.
